{{for|the historian|Dieter Pohl (historian)}}
{{Use mdy dates|date=December 2015}}
'''Dieter Pohl''' (Wolfgang Dieter Pohl, born 1938) is a German–Swiss physicist. He became known especially for his pioneering works in [[nano-optics]], [[near field optics]] (NFO), and [[plasmonics]].[[File:Dieter Pohl, Physiker.jpg|thumb|Dieter Pohl, physicist]]

Pohl studied at the [[University of Stuttgart]] and the [[Technical University of Munich]] (TUM) where he did his doctorate with [[Wolfgang Kaiser (Physiker)|Wolfgang Kaiser]]. In 1968, he moved to [[IBM Zurich Research Laboratory]] in Rüschlikon and 1998 to [[University of Basel]]. He was appointed titular professor in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.unibas.ch/index.cfm?uuid=F9F2BCED0B8F50D65E68042B1FD4D910&type=search&show_long=1|title=Meldung der Universität Basel über neue Titularprofessoren|publisher=University of Basel | date=November 15, 2002 |access-date=April 5, 2019| archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141013211826/https://www.unibas.ch/index.cfm?uuid=F9F2BCED0B8F50D65E68042B1FD4D910&type=search&show_long=1 | archive-date= October 13, 2014 }}</ref>

In 1982, he invented and developed the [[NSOM|near-field scanning optical microscopy (NSOM/SNOM)]].,<ref>Dieter W. Pohl ''Optical near field scanning microscope'', US-Patent Nr. 4604520, 1982, EP patent 0112401, [http://worldwide.espacenet.com/publicationDetails/biblio?CC=EP&NR=0112401&KC=&FT=E&locale=en_EP Abstract]</ref> the first optical instrument that provided optical resolution far beyond Abbe's diffraction limit, e.g. 20&nbsp;nm at wavelength 515&nbsp;nm.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pohl |first1=D. W. |last2=Denk |first2=W. |last3=Lanz |first3=M. |title=Optical stethoscopy: Image recording with resolution λ/20 |journal=[[Applied Physics Letters]] |year=1984 |volume=44 |issue=7 |pages=651–653 |doi=10.1063/1.94865|bibcode=1984ApPhL..44..651P |doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Dürig |first1=U. |last2=Pohl |first2=D. W. |last3=Rohner |first3=F. |title=Near-field optical-scanning microscopy |journal=[[Journal of Applied Physics]] |year=1986 |volume=59 |issue=10 |pages=3318–3327 |doi=10.1063/1.336848|bibcode=1986JAP....59.3318D }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Denk |first1=Winfried |title=Near-field optics: Microscopy with nanometer-size fields |journal=[[Journal of Vacuum Science & Technology B]] |year= 1991 |volume=9 |issue=2 |pages=510–513 |doi=10.1116/1.585558|bibcode=1991JVSTB...9..510D }}</ref><ref>D. W. Pohl ''Scanning Near-Field Optical Microscopy'', in Optical and Electron Microscopy Vol. 12, 243 – 312, Academic Press New York 1991</ref>
In the following years the close relation between optical near-fields and plasmons was investigated,<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fischer |first1=U. Ch. |last2=Pohl |first2=D. W. |title=Observation of Single-Particle Plasmons by Near-Field Optical Microscopy |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |year=1989 |volume=62 |issue=4 |pages=458–461 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.62.458|pmid=10040238 |bibcode=1989PhRvL..62..458F }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Hecht |first1=B. |last2=Bielefeldt |first2=H. |last3=Novotny |first3=L. |last4=Inouye |first4=Y. |last5=Pohl |first5=D. W. |title=Local Excitation, Scattering, and Interference of Surface Plasmons |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |year=1996 |volume=77 |issue=9 |pages=1889–1892 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.77.1889|pmid=10063197 |bibcode=1996PhRvL..77.1889H }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Bouhelier |first1=A. |last2=Huser |first2=Th. |last3=Tamaru |first3=H. |last4=Güntherodt |first4=H.-J. |last5=Pohl |first5=D. W. |last6=Baida |first6=Fadi I. |last7=Van Labeke |first7=D. |title=Plasmon optics of structured silver films |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |year=2001 |volume=63 |issue=15 |article-number=155404 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.63.155404|bibcode=2001PhRvB..63o5404B }}</ref> contributing to the emergence of the new field of [[plasmonics]].

1999 Dieter Pohl suggested antennas as ideal sources or probes of localized  optical near-fields.<ref>D. W. Pohl ''Near field optics seen as an antenna problem'' in Near-Field Optics: Principles and Applications / The Second Asia-Pacific Workshop on Near Field Optics, Beijing, China October 20–23, 1999, EDITOR M. Ohtsu and X. Zhu,(World Scientific, {{ISBN|981-02-4365-0}}, Singapore, p.9 – 21), 2000</ref> 
The problem was that ''optical antennas'' have to be 1000000 times smaller than the TV antennas one can see on any roof. By 2005, Dieter and his coworkers<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Muhlschlegel |first1=P. |title=Resonant Optical Antennas |journal=[[Science (journal)|Science]] |year=2005 |volume=308 |issue=5728 |pages=1607–1609 |doi=10.1126/science.1111886|pmid=15947182 |bibcode=2005Sci...308.1607M |s2cid=40214874 |url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/164842 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Farahani |first1=J. N. |last2=Pohl |first2=D. W. |last3=Eisler |first3=H.-J. |last4=Hecht |first4=B. |title=Single Quantum Dot Coupled to a Scanning Optical Antenna: A Tunable Superemitter |journal=[[Physical Review Letters]] |year=2005 |volume=95 |issue=1 |article-number=017402 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.95.017402|pmid=16090656 |bibcode=2005PhRvL..95a7402F }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Farahani |first1=Javad N |last2=Eisler |first2=Hans-Jürgen |last3=Pohl |first3=Dieter W |last4=Pavius |first4=Michaël |last5=Flückiger |first5=Philippe |last6=Gasser |first6=Philippe |last7=Hecht |first7=Bert |title=Bow-tie optical antenna probes for single-emitter scanning near-field optical microscopy |journal=[[Nanotechnology (journal)|Nanotechnology]] |year=2007 |volume=18 |issue=12 |article-number=125506 |doi=10.1088/0957-4484/18/12/125506|bibcode=2007Nanot..18l5506F |s2cid=18395179 |url=https://infoscience.epfl.ch/record/101154 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Pohl |first1=Dieter W. |last2=Rodrigo |first2=Sergio G. |last3=Novotny |first3=Lukas |title=Stacked optical antennas |journal=[[Applied Physics Letters]] |year=2011 |volume=98 |issue=2 |page=023111 |doi=10.1063/1.3541544|bibcode=2011ApPhL..98b3111P |doi-access=free |hdl=10261/369900 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> had solved the problem and could demonstrate for the first time the resonance and lifetime-reducing properties of nanometer-sized [[dipole antenna]]s as well as an extremely high local intensity in the (antenna) gap, the place where the wires of a TV antenna are fixed. The intensity caused higher order nonlinear light emission, an interesting fact in view of the tiny near-field spot.

In 1992, Dieter Pohl and Daniel Courjon organized a workshop on near-field optics (NFO)<ref>Dieter W. Pohl and Daniel Courjon, "Near Field Optics", NATO ASI SeriesKluwer Academic 1993, {{ISBN|0-7923-2394-7}}</ref> that was to become the origin of bi-annual international NFO-x conferences (2018: x = 15), a platform for nano-, near-field-, nonlinear optics, plasmonics, metamaterials, quantum information, biosensing and ultrafast dynamics.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://nfo15.utt.fr/ | title=NFO15 - 15th international conference on Near-field Optics and Nanophotonics | date=2018 | access-date=April 5, 2019}}</ref>

Dieter Pohl contributed to various reviews and book publications. He acted as reviewer for the [[Swiss National Science Foundation]] (SNF) and the German [[Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft|DFG]].  A complete list<ref name="Publications and Patents">{{cite web | url=https://www.physik.unibas.ch/fileadmin/user_upload/physik-unibas-ch/06_People/06_Emeriti/PohlDieter_2017_Complete_list_of_Publications.pdf | title=Dieter W. Pohl: Publications and Patents | publisher=Department of Physics, University of Basel | date=2017 | access-date=April 5, 2019}}</ref> of his papers and inventions will be found on his home page.<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.physik.unibas.ch/de/personen/list-prof-emeriti/prof-emer-pohl.html | title=Prof. Emer. Pohl | access-date=September 15, 2018 | archive-date=April 17, 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180417111305/https://www.physik.unibas.ch/de/personen/list-prof-emeriti/prof-emer-pohl.html }}</ref>

;Publications and Patents

≈121 publications

≈20 patents, mostly on scanning probe microscopy, micromechanics, storage; diverse publications in the ''[[IBM Technical Disclosure Bulletin]]''

;Awards and Honors

* 1996 Carl-Zeiss Research Award
* 1997 Rank Prize for Electro-Optics
* 1999 Humboldt Research Prize
* 1968-1998 various IBM internal awards
* 2013 [[Stern-Gerlach Medal]] of the German Physical Society<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.dpg-physik.de/auszeichnungen/dpg-preise/stern-gerlach-medaille/preistraeger | title=Prizewinners - Stern Gerlach Medal | publisher=German Physical Society | access-date=April 5, 2019}}</ref>
